A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AURA method and AmodalReasonSeg research. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's supplementary Sections 7–10. The supplied v1 contains no supplementary appendix.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 report original segmentation comparisons, qualitative predictions and ablations on AmodalReasonSeg, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds a qualitative RICE evaluation and training/inference efficiency comparisons in the supplement.

M1.justification: The dual mask decoders, occlusion encoders, LoRA adaptation and losses remain unchanged. The added linear/sigmoid description in Section 3.3 clarifies components already depicted in Figure 3; the supplement uses the same architecture.

E1.justification: Section 7 adds a limited remote-sensing extension using ten annotated RICE images to segment land and rivers under cloud occlusion. This introduces a distinct input domain, but remains an illustrative supplement; the main AmodalReasonSeg coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same three amodal methods, six MLLM methods and internal baseline. The added efficiency comparison reuses LISA. New dagger annotations for amodal methods clarify the separate visible/amodal training already described in v1.

E3.justification: The new RICE experiment fine-tunes on eight images and validates on two, using the main model settings. Section 8.2 adds inference-throughput evaluation. Existing AmodalReasonSeg splits, metrics, backbones and training budgets remain unchanged; additional baseline-scoring descriptions disclose previously unspecified details.

E4.justification: v2 adds an exploratory cross-domain qualitative study in Section 7/Figure 6 and a training/inference efficiency analysis in Section 8.2. The occlusion-module, LoRA and backbone ablations in Tables 2–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Training methods twice refers to separate visible and amodal supervision, not statistical repetitions.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. v2 adds LISA's eight-hour training time per mask type alongside AURA's previously reported ten hours for both, throughput of 0.33 fps for LISA versus 0.28 fps for AURA, and the qualitative RICE prediction in Figure 6.

T1.justification: The task definition, spatial occlusion-map definition and loss equations (1)–(4) are retained. The supplementary task distinctions are conceptual explanations; no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: amodal reasoning segmentation, AmodalReasonSeg, and AURA's joint visible/amodal prediction with occlusion learning. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds interpretations concerning remote-sensing applicability while explicitly qualifying the cloud example as illustrative, qualitative and outside the core evaluation. The conclusion adds future directions concerning inference efficiency and dataset diversity and granularity.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the release promise with a reported release and project-page link, supplies the full GPT-4o generation prompt in Figure 7, and documents initialization, baseline-scoring rules and annotation revision/supplementation. These substantially expand reproducibility information for the existing dataset and experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning RICE, Landsat, 3D activity reasoning, compression and video quality, and removes Ao et al.'s Open-world amodal appearance completion citation. Section 9.3 explicitly relates the internal baseline to modified LISA; the main related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections, adds author contacts and acknowledgments, and appends supplementary explanations of task distinctions, evaluation and dataset construction. Main Sections 1–6 retain their organization and largely their wording.

P2.justification: Figures 6–9 substantially expand the visual documentation with a cloud-occlusion result, the complete generation prompt and two illustrated dataset examples. Figures 1–5 retain identical artwork, although some displays are resized; tables are compressed and Figure 5's caption clarifies that the displayed answers are ground truth.

improvement.justification: The prompt, annotation explanations, baseline-scoring details and resource link improve transparency and reproducibility, while efficiency measurements add practical evidence. The gains are limited: the core benchmark results are unchanged, and the RICE extension provides only qualitative evidence after fine-tuning, with two validation images. Overall, v2 makes the existing work easier to assess without substantially strengthening its empirical conclusions.
